provenance.instrument: Clifton Heights Borough Zoning Ordinance of 1993 (Chapter 340 Zoning, Ord. No. 729 of 3-22-1993, as amended), with Chapter 165 Floodplain Management (Ord. No. 846 of 10-20-2015), as published on eCode360
provenance.status_detail: eCode360 CL3044, Borough of Clifton Heights, PA. 340-112A sends appeals to the Court of Common Pleas of Delaware County and 340-115D(2) uses the Delaware County Tax Assessment Office, so this is Clifton Heights borough, Delaware County. The district use lists and figures are web text in each district article. Attachment 1 (Appendix A, C-1 areas), Attachment 2 (Zoning Requirements) and Attachment 3 (Table of Permitted Uses) are PDF summaries that were not opened. The latest amendments seen are Ord. Nos. 866, 868 and 869 of 2019. New Laws lists no new law
provenance.code_current_through_note: eCode360 shows 'Includes legislation through 12-17-2019.' New Laws: 'There are currently no known new laws for this Code.'
provenance.code_caution: The online code includes legislation only through 12-17-2019. Its New Laws list is empty, and no later zoning amendment was found, but one may exist. Ask the borough office whether Chapter 340 has changed since 2019
checks: The code has no accessory dwelling unit use. A search for accessory dwelling, in-law, accessory apartment, second dwelling, ECHO, guest house, living quarters, conversion, two-family, granny, elder cottage, temporary dwelling and apartment found the dwelling and conversion definitions, the R-2 and R-3 two-family listings and the I district conversion of industrial buildings (340-53C)

R-1 is used 'by right only' for a single-family detached dwelling and municipal uses, with schools, religious uses, day care, clubs and cluster development by special exception (340-14, 340-15). R-2 adds semidetached, attached (at most five in a row) and two-family dwellings of three kinds, including 'Two-family detached or a duplex dwelling containing no more than two single-family dwellings' (340-19). R-3 adds multifamily dwellings on one acre (340-24). The RCZ cluster option is a special exception in R-1, R-2 and R-3 on a tract of at least one acre in single and separate ownership, for the residential uses R-1, R-2 and R-3 permit by right, with no structure within 30 ft of a lot line and no more units than the underlying district allows (340-15E, 340-28A, 340-29, 340-31, see the other paths). RCD permits recreation uses, with low-density single-family dwellings at seven units per acre by special exception (340-35, 340-36). C-1, C-2 and I list no dwelling

Accessory uses in the residential districts are parking and private garages, 'Utility sheds, toolsheds and similar accessory structures', pools, signs, home occupations and decks (340-16, 340-21, 340-26). A dwelling unit is 'One or more rooms designed constituting a separate housekeeping unit which, at a minimum, must include cooking, sleeping and sanitary facilities'. A family is persons related by blood, marriage or adoption, or no more than three unrelated persons, living as a single housekeeping unit (340-12). A lot is 'A parcel of land on which a main building and any accessory buildings are or may be placed', and an accessory building is one 'customarily incidental and subordinate to the principal building' (340-12). A detached dwelling is not a customary accessory building, so a second detached dwelling would be a second main building on the lot. A conversion is 'Any change of use or physical layout of a structure from which it was originally intended' (340-12), and a change of use needs a permit and must conform to the chapter (340-75A, 340-92A)

Accessory structures together cover at most 5% of the lot in residential districts, so 250 sq ft on a 5,000 sq ft lot (340-80A(1)). They are at most one story or 14 ft tall, stand at least 3 ft from the side and rear lines 'and behind the rearmost portion of the principal building', and on a corner lot no closer to the side street than the house (340-80). The district sections keep them out of the required front yard and 5 ft from any property line, reducible to 3 ft by special exception (340-17I, 340-22J, 340-27J). The district sections were amended later, in 2019, so their 5 ft is the yard by right, and 3 ft is the least the Board may grant

Lot area: 5,000 sq ft per single-family detached dwelling in R-1, 3,000 sq ft per dwelling unit for residential uses in R-2, the R-2 figure in R-3 except 1,500 sq ft per unit for attached and multifamily uses (340-17A, 340-22A, 340-27A). In R-1 'for all other uses' the minimum is 10,000 sq ft. Side yards for a detached house are two, with an aggregate of 20 ft and neither under 8 ft. In R-2 a semidetached house and the end unit of an attached row have one side yard of at least 12 ft, in R-3 10 ft. An interior unit of a row has no side yard (340-17G, 340-22G, 340-27G). A lot held in single and separate ownership when the chapter took effect may be built on below the minimum area or width if the use, yard, setback and density rules are met (340-102). Since the density rules must still be met, a two-family dwelling on such a lot is read to need 3,000 sq ft per unit

Parking: 'Single-family dwelling, 2 per dwelling unit', and for multifamily and townhouses 1 space for an efficiency, 2 for one or two bedrooms and 3 for three or more. Only a fraction of 1/2 or more counts as a space. The table has no two-family row. Parking is on the same lot except in C-1. A use changed or extended so that it needs more parking provides the added spaces (340-67C, 340-68)

Floodplain (Chapter 165, FIRM of November 18, 2009, applied through 340-8): a permit is needed for any construction or development anywhere in the borough, and development includes renovation, repair, expansion or alteration of buildings. New construction and substantial improvements of residential structures are elevated to the base flood elevation plus 1 1/2 ft, basements are prohibited, and an accessory structure that is not elevated is not used for habitation and is at most 200 sq ft. In the floodway nothing may raise flood levels and new construction needs a DEP permit. Manufactured homes are prohibited unless a variance is granted, and never within 50 ft of the top of bank. Floodplain variances are considered by the Borough under the procedure of 165-17, which sends appeals to the Zoning Hearing Board. The code does not name the body outright. No variance may raise the base flood elevation (165-8, 165-17, 165-19, 165-24, 165-28, 165-33, 165-34, 165-36 'Development')

Riparian buffer: 'The riparian buffer shall be maintained within 100 feet of the top of stream bank and shall remain as open, undeveloped area' (340-87G). The buffer reaches 100 ft from the top of bank 'or to the limit of the 100-year floodplain, whichever distance is greater' (340-12 'Riparian buffers'). Stormwater easements, rights-of-way, surface water, wetlands and steep slopes (over 15%) are deducted in full, and riparian buffers and wetland buffers by half, from the area used for total improvement coverage (340-12 'Total improvement area'). No steep slope or wetland chapter was found in Chapter 340

Special exceptions are granted only where the district article provides for them, with an environmental impact assessment and a traffic impact study (340-114, 340-90, 340-90.1). A use variance also needs an environmental impact assessment (340-90A). Variances go to the Zoning Hearing Board on the MPC findings, and lapse without a building permit within six months (340-105C, 340-109A, 340-111). No bar on a use variance was found

Nonconforming uses and structures may be enlarged by special exception once, by at most 50%, within the district's area, height and setback rules (340-98). In I, the conversion of existing industrial buildings to residential units is a special exception (340-53C). A nonconforming structure or use may also get a temporary permit by special exception for up to two years (340-92F). That is not a path for a second unit

path.note: A second unit on a single-family lot is not a listed use, so the path is a use variance from the Zoning Hearing Board (MPC 910.2). In R-2 and R-3 a house may instead become a two-family dwelling by right where the lot has 3,000 sq ft per unit (see the other paths)

fallback_path.note: Zoning Hearing Board on the MPC findings. No bar on a use variance was found

unlisted_use_path.note: Only I lets the Zoning Hearing Board allow a use of the same general character as its listed industrial and service uses. RCD allows a use of the same general character as its recreation uses by conditional use (340-35.1B). Elsewhere a use not listed needs a use variance. I lists no dwelling, while R-2 and R-3 list two-family dwellings, so in those districts a second unit is read as that listed use, not an unlisted one

unlisted_use_districts.note: The other districts are used 'by right only' for their listed uses

unlisted_use_scope.quote: Those uses not specifically permitted by right, but of the same general character as those listed in § 340-52 above

value.name: Two-family dwelling (R-2, R-3)
value.conditions: R-2 permits by right a 'Two-family detached or a duplex dwelling containing no more than two single-family dwellings', a two-family semidetached dwelling and a two-family attached dwelling, and R-3 permits every R-2 use. The lot needs 3,000 sq ft per dwelling unit, so 6,000 sq ft for two units, and a two-family detached dwelling 50 ft of width. A two-family detached dwelling has two side yards, neither under 8 ft and 20 ft together. A two-family semidetached dwelling and the end unit of a two-family attached row have one side yard, 12 ft in R-2 and 10 ft in R-3. Front 20 ft, rear 25 ft, building coverage 30% in R-2 and 50% in R-3, height 35 ft. Parking is 2 spaces per single-family dwelling unit and the table has no two-family row. A changed or extended use provides the added parking. Each unit has its own cooking, sleeping and sanitary facilities
value.note: The code has no conversion section. It defines a conversion as 'Any change of use or physical layout of a structure from which it was originally intended' (340-12), and a change of use must conform to the chapter and needs a permit (340-75A, 340-92A). So whether an existing house may be changed into a two-family dwelling under these listings is read from those sections. Ask the zoning officer

value.name: RCZ cluster development (R-1, R-2, R-3)
value.conditions: The cluster option is 'permitted by special exception as an option in the R-1, R-2, and R-3 Residential Districts'. It may hold the residential uses R-1, R-2 and R-3 permit by right, so in R-1 also the two-family dwellings of R-2. The tract is at least one acre in single and separate ownership. No structure stands within 30 ft of any lot line, the underlying district's height applies, and the number of units may not exceed what the underlying district allows (in R-1 5,000 sq ft per single-family detached dwelling and 10,000 sq ft for all other uses). Open space is set aside for perpetual preservation. The Zoning Hearing Board needs an environmental impact assessment and a traffic impact study
value.note: A cluster development of a whole tract, not a unit added to one house lot. Ask the zoning officer

districts_read_no_listing.note: None lists an accessory dwelling unit. R-2 and R-3 list two-family dwellings. RCD lists low-density single-family dwellings by special exception, and I the conversion of industrial buildings to residential units by special exception

value.condition: In the identified floodplain an accessory structure that is not elevated or floodproofed 'shall not be designed or used for human habitation', is limited to parking or storage, has at most 200 sq ft of floor area and no sanitary facilities or permanently affixed utility equipment. Floodplain variances are considered by the Borough under the procedure of 165-17, which sends appeals to the Zoning Hearing Board, and no variance may raise the base flood elevation.

In the identified floodplain any new construction or substantial improvement of a residential structure has its lowest floor, basement included, at or above the regulatory flood elevation, the base flood elevation plus 1 1/2 ft, and basements are prohibited. Work under 50% of market value is elevated or floodproofed to the greatest extent possible. No expansion of an existing structure may raise the base flood elevation. New construction is a structure begun on or after September 1, 2015, with its later improvements.

In the floodway no encroachment, fill, new construction, substantial improvement or other development is permitted unless a hydrologic and hydraulic analysis shows no increase in flood levels, and no new construction or development without a permit from the DEP Regional Office.

'The riparian buffer shall be maintained within 100 feet of the top of stream bank and shall remain as open, undeveloped area.' A new building or addition for the unit cannot stand within 100 ft of the top of a stream bank. The buffer is the greater of 100 ft from the top of bank or the limit of the 100-year floodplain, so where the 100-year floodplain reaches farther, the buffer does too.

A riparian buffer reaches 'to the limit of the 100-year floodplain' where that is farther than 100 ft from the top of bank, and the buffer 'shall remain as open, undeveloped area'. On a lot in the identified floodplain a new building or addition for the unit may stand in the buffer, where it is barred.

disputed_by.note: Only the land within 100 ft of the top of bank, or out to the limit of the 100-year floodplain, is buffer. A lot in the identified floodplain may still have its building spot outside the floodplain and more than 100 ft from the top of bank, and there the buffer does not reach it
